_comment: Boolean pharmacological facts read by an engine, never rendered as a UI chip (that is what `tags` is for). Keys are substances.canonical_name; each entry lists the flags that substance carries.

_flags.suppresses-serotonin-synthesis: Metabolites suppress tryptophan hydroxylase, so the SERT class's slow synthesis pool recovers on a weeks-scale clock instead of the days-scale reset of the synthesis-sparing releasers (Specs/tolerance-faithful-model-improvements.md §3.4). Methylenedioxy entactogens only — the cathinone releasers (mephedrone and relatives) spare synthesis and must NOT carry this flag.
_flags.missold-as-mdma: Frequently pressed and sold as MDMA or "molly" while being a pharmacologically DAT-dominant reuptake blocker: longer, more stimulant and anxiogenic, and more dangerous on an empathogen-style redose. A market fact about what the pill contains, so it is carried per substance rather than inferred from the binding profile — the profile is what makes the substitution dangerous, not what identifies it.
_flags.model-calibrated: The effect model was actually calibrated against human data for this substance, so a session containing it may surface Effect Estimates. Every other modelable substance (methamphetamine, cocaine, kratom, MDMA, …) is still read as an interacting agent that shapes the aggregate curves — the flag gates whether a substance can ANCHOR a simulation on its own, not whether the engine can simulate it. A substance earns this only when human dose-response data anchored its parameters; the cathinones rest on a human 3-MMC study.
